office_does: A Metropolitan King County Councilmember writes county law and adopts the county budget, which covers public health, behavioral health, Metro transit, regional homelessness and housing, and services for unincorporated areas.
race_blurb: Incumbent Teresa Mosqueda, a former Seattle councilmember who led passage of the JumpStart payroll tax, faces first-time candidate Nick Duda, who runs on audits, measurable outcomes and treatment-required paths off the street. Mosqueda took 66% of the August primary vote to Duda's 25%.

candidates.summary: Incumbent District 8 councilmember since 2024 and chair of the King County Board of Health, after about seven years on the Seattle City Council; backed by Democratic organizations and labor unions.
highlights: Pamphlet priorities: affordable housing and anti-displacement, community safety through behavioral health and gun-violence prevention, and transit, childcare and healthcare for working families [S1]
As Board of Health chair, called in September 2026 for using state-authorized property-tax tools to backfill federal Medicaid cuts to public health and Harborview [S5]
Co-sponsored and voted for council motions opposing initiatives IL26-638 and IL26-001, which passed 7-2 on Sept. 22, 2026 [S6][S7][S8][S9]
Listed on the Vote No on I-645 coalition page [S11]
Led passage of Seattle's JumpStart payroll tax and sponsored the county ban on rent price-fixing algorithms [S2]

taxes.basis: Passed Seattle's JumpStart payroll tax, calls for activating new property-tax authority for public health and Harborview, and is on the No on I-645 (income-tax repeal) coalition.

spending.basis: Platform and record center on expanding investment in housing, behavioral health, public health, childcare and transit, including a budget amendment to backfill federal housing cuts and a call to invest new revenue in the health safety net.

housing.basis: Prioritizes public investment in affordable and supportive housing and anti-displacement, and sponsored the county ban on rent price-fixing algorithms (tenant protection).

safety.basis: Frames community safety around behavioral health investment and gun-violence prevention; no enforcement-first proposals in the dossier.

climate.basis: Co-sponsored the county's Strategic Climate Action Plan update and lists green housing among her priorities; climate is not a lead campaign theme.

experience.basis: Ten years of elected legislative service (Seattle City Council, then King County Council) with enacted housing and labor legislation.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and self-described lifelong Democrat with 17 years in private-sector data and analytics work and about 10 months as a Seattle City Council policy aide; endorsed by the Seattle Times in the primary.
highlights: Argues the region's results on homelessness, overdoses and property crime 'aren't for lack of funding' and calls for audits, measurable goals and published results [S1][S3]
Supports 'treatment-required paths off the street', stabilization centers, sober housing, and escalating consequences for chronic and organized offenders [S1][S3]
Proposes fixing permitting, more density near light rail stations, and fare gates with reduced fares [S1][S3]
No public position found on I-645, I-001 or I-638 [S7][S8]

spending.basis: Central message in pamphlet and campaign site is outcome measurement, audits and contract oversight over spending more ('Good government isn't measured by how much we spend').

taxes.basis: Pamphlet says the region has 'consistently increased taxes' and residents are 'being taxed out of your home'; no specific tax proposal or tax-cut plan.

housing.basis: Housing plan leads with permitting fixes, fewer construction barriers and substantially more density near stations, alongside 'safe and stabilizing' public housing.

safety.basis: Treatment-required paths off the street, escalating consequences for chronic offenders and a 'three strikes' path to mandatory treatment, paired with diversion 'where appropriate' and victim services.

experience.basis: Never held office; brings private-sector experience and under a year as a council policy aide rather than a governing record.
